seo.title: Homeless and housing-crisis help in Edmonton - No Home Help
seo.description: Current Edmonton contacts for emergency shelter access, day services, food, health care, benefits, jobs and other help for people without stable housing.

page.heading: Homeless and housing-crisis help in Edmonton
page.urgent: Immediate danger, serious injury, overdose, fire or a crime in progress: call 911. For non-emergency crisis outreach and transport to a safe place, call 211 and press 3.
page.notice: Shelters and services can be full, change hours or require an assessment or referral. Call before travelling whenever possible. No listing guarantees a bed, housing, treatment, benefits or a job.
page.intro: If one shelter is full, call 211 and try the other local options below. Say your age, who is with you, whether you have a pet, and any health, safety, accessibility or cultural needs. Ask about outreach, transport, day services and the next safe option rather than relying on one address.
page.footer: No Home Help is independent of the City, Province and service providers. Confirm capacity and intake rules before travelling.

entries.title: Coordinated Access
entries.description: Housing and shelter navigation for people experiencing homelessness. An assessment can open referrals but does not guarantee same-day placement.

entries.title: 911 — emergency services
entries.description: Call for immediate danger, serious injury, overdose, fire or another life-threatening emergency.

entries.title: 211 Alberta — local service referrals
entries.description: Free, confidential navigation for shelter, meals, health, housing and social services. Ask the navigator to check several alternatives when one service is full.
entries.how_to_access: Call 211, text INFO to 211 or use online chat.

entries.title: 211, press 3 — Crisis Diversion Team
entries.description: Non-emergency crisis response for a person outside who needs help reaching a safe place. Teams can assess needs and may provide transport. Response and destination depend on urgency and availability.
entries.how_to_access: Call 211 and press 3. Give the exact location and describe the person's condition. Call 911 instead for immediate danger or urgent medical need.

entries.title: Bissell Centre — West Navigation and Support Centre
entries.description: Walk-in navigation, housing assessment and referrals for adults without stable housing. Staff can check current shelter options, but a visit does not guarantee a bed.
entries.how_to_access: Call before travelling and ask for coordinated-access alternatives if shelters are full.

entries.title: Hope Mission — emergency shelter and meals
entries.description: Emergency accommodation, meals and support for adults. Capacity and intake rules change; call first and ask what to do if no bed is available.
entries.hours: Call for current shelter intake; the community hub operates daily
entries.how_to_access: Call or check the official page before travelling. Capacity is not guaranteed; ask about eligibility, documents, referral rules and an alternative if the service is full.

entries.title: Hope Mission — Herb Jamieson Centre
entries.description: Year-round emergency accommodation in Edmonton. Capacity and the population served can change, so confirm the current intake route before travelling.
entries.how_to_access: Call Hope Mission or 211 for current availability and intake instructions.

entries.title: e4c Women's Emergency Accommodation Centre
entries.description: Year-round emergency shelter for women experiencing homelessness, with housing-focused support. A bed is not guaranteed.
entries.how_to_access: Call before travelling or ask 211 to confirm the current intake process and availability.

entries.title: Wîhcihaw Maskokamik — Indigenous-led shelter
entries.description: Year-round emergency accommodation operated with Enoch Cree Nation. Ask about current eligibility, cultural supports and available space.
entries.how_to_access: Call the shelter or 211 before travelling.

entries.title: YESS — youth emergency shelter
entries.description: Emergency shelter, meals, basic needs and trauma-informed support for youth. YESS also has daytime programs for ages 15 to 24.
entries.how_to_access: Call extension 231 and confirm age eligibility and current space before travelling.

entries.title: St. Katherine Drexel Family Shelter — referral only
entries.description: Emergency accommodation for families. The provincial shelter directory states that admission is by referral rather than direct walk-in.
entries.how_to_access: Call and ask which agency can make the required referral. Do not travel expecting a walk-in bed.

entries.title: Hope Mission Community Hub — free meals
entries.description: Free community meals at the Bruce Reith Centre; people do not have to be shelter guests. The provider publishes three meals on weekdays and brunch and dinner on weekends.
entries.hours: Meal schedule published on the provider page
entries.how_to_access: Walk in for the published meal time; call before a long journey because serving arrangements can change.

entries.title: Edmonton's Food Bank — food hampers
entries.description: Request an emergency food hamper and find other food support. Registration, pickup location and timing depend on the current process.
entries.address: Pickup location provided during the request process
entries.hours: Check current request and pickup hours
entries.how_to_access: Use the official request process or call client services. Ask what identification is accepted and when the hamper can be collected.

entries.title: Edmonton's Food Bank — current free-meal map
entries.description: Official list and map of free community meals across Edmonton. Listed meals require no appointment, registration or identification, but schedules vary by partner.
entries.how_to_access: Check the current map immediately before travelling and choose a second option in case a meal is cancelled or reaches capacity.

entries.title: Hope Mission Community Hub — hygiene and laundry
entries.description: Open community hub with hygiene, laundry, meals, health, ID, income and housing support. Services are available beyond shelter guests.
entries.hours: Check the current daily service schedule
entries.how_to_access: Ask the hub about shower or laundry sign-up and the last service time.

entries.title: Bissell Centre Community Space — showers, laundry and clothing
entries.description: Low-barrier community space providing practical supports including showers, laundry, food, clothing, mail and connections to case workers. Renovations can move services within the building.
entries.how_to_access: Use the open entrance and ask reception where each service is operating that day.

entries.title: Bissell Centre — Community Closet
entries.description: Donated clothing and basic items for community members. Stock, sizes and location inside the building can change during renovations.
entries.how_to_access: Ask reception about Community Closet access and alternatives if the needed item is unavailable.

entries.title: 988 Suicide Crisis Helpline
entries.description: Call or text 988 for crisis support. Call 911 for immediate danger.

entries.title: Radius Community Health & Healing — barrier-free primary care
entries.description: No-cost primary, mental and addiction health services for people facing barriers including poverty, homelessness and lack of identification. Minor urgent problems may be assessed, subject to eligibility and capacity.
entries.how_to_access: Phone or drop in for a new-patient assessment. Call 911 for a life-threatening emergency.

entries.title: Radius Dental Clinic — care for people facing barriers
entries.description: Dental care for people unable to access treatment because of homelessness, low income, mental illness, addiction or other barriers. Subsidy eligibility requires assessment and proof of income.
entries.how_to_access: Call for an appointment. The clinic tries to accommodate dental emergencies and weekday walk-ins but cannot guarantee same-day care.

entries.title: Access 24/7 — addiction and mental-health access
entries.description: Adult service navigation, screening, assessment, referral, crisis intervention, outreach and short-term stabilization for Edmonton residents.
entries.address: Edmonton Community Health Hub North, 13211 Fort Road NW, Edmonton, AB
entries.how_to_access: Call or go to the access site. Call 911 for immediate danger or a life-threatening emergency.

entries.title: George Spady Society — medically supported detox
entries.description: Medically supported setting for withdrawal, health stabilization and connection to recovery services. Admission depends on triage and capacity.
entries.address: 15625 Stony Plain Road NW, southwest entrance, Edmonton, AB
entries.how_to_access: Call before travelling and arrive for triage as instructed. Call 911 for a medical emergency.

entries.title: Bissell Centre Community Space — day services
entries.description: Indoor community space with food, hygiene, clothing, mail, basic support and case-worker connections. It is not an overnight shelter.
entries.hours: Call for current hours during renovations
entries.how_to_access: Walk in through the available entrance and ask reception for the service needed.

entries.title: Ride Transit Program — reduced fares
entries.description: Reduced Edmonton Transit fares for eligible low-income residents. Application processing can take several weeks and identification or income documents are required.
entries.address: Apply online, by mail or at the Edmonton Service Centre
entries.how_to_access: Check the current income limits and documents. Ask a navigation worker for help if identification is a barrier.

entries.title: Government of Canada Benefits Finder
entries.description: Official questionnaire for federal and provincial benefits. It does not guarantee approval or immediate money.

entries.title: Alberta Supports — income and disability programs
entries.description: Provincial help navigating Income Support, AISH and many other benefits. Services are available by phone and online in more than 100 languages.
entries.address: Online and at Edmonton Alberta Supports centres
entries.how_to_access: Call for program screening and application help. Approval and payment are not guaranteed.

entries.title: Alberta emergency financial assistance
entries.description: One-time, short-term help may be available for urgent food, temporary shelter, transportation, medication or medical supplies when other resources cannot be used. Eligibility is assessed by the Province.
entries.how_to_access: Pre-apply online when instructed and call to complete the assessment. Explain the immediate need and why it cannot wait.

entries.title: Job Bank
entries.description: Official job search, employment service and training information across Canada.

entries.title: Bent Arrow — Indigenous employment and housing support
entries.description: Culturally grounded services for Indigenous children, youth, adults and families, including employment services and Indigenous Housing First support.
entries.how_to_access: Call and ask for the employment or housing program that fits your situation. Confirm eligibility and appointment requirements.

entries.title: Edmonton Community Legal Centre — free legal help
entries.description: Free legal information and advice for eligible low-income people in landlord and tenant, employment, human rights, debt, family, immigration, small claims and income-support matters.
entries.hours: Call for intake and eligibility screening
entries.how_to_access: Call as early as possible when there is an eviction, appeal or court deadline.

entries.title: Navigation and Support Centre — identification help
entries.description: Walk-in help obtaining identification, accessing income support and connecting to emergency shelter and housing. The service is pet-friendly.
entries.address: Bissell Centre West, 10530 96 Street NW, Edmonton, AB
entries.how_to_access: Walk in before the cutoff and bring any documents or photographs of documents available.

entries.title: Bissell Centre — mailing address and mail pickup
entries.description: Community members can use Bissell Centre as a mailing address for government documents, identification applications, tax returns and personal mail. Regular mail service continues during renovations.
entries.hours: Call for registration and pickup hours
entries.how_to_access: Ask reception how to register the address and exactly how your name must appear on incoming mail.

entries.title: Bridge Housing — short-term housing with private storage
entries.description: Referral-based stays of roughly 21 to 90 days with meals, showers, laundry, private storage and housing support while moving toward permanent housing.
entries.address: Placement arranged through a Coordinated Access partner
entries.how_to_access: Contact Homeward Trust Coordinated Access or an agency screening partner. Placement is not immediate or guaranteed.

entries.title: WIN House — shelter from gender-based violence
entries.description: Two emergency shelters and a second-stage shelter for women, children and gender-diverse people fleeing violence. Shelter addresses are confidential.
entries.hours: Call for immediate safety planning and space
entries.how_to_access: Call the shelter line. Call 911 for immediate danger.

entries.title: Lurana Shelter — women and children fleeing violence
entries.description: Emergency shelter and support for women and children leaving domestic or family violence. The location is confidential.
entries.how_to_access: Call for safety planning and shelter availability. Call 911 for immediate danger.

entries.title: Bent Arrow — Indigenous Housing First
entries.description: Culturally grounded housing and wraparound support for Indigenous people experiencing chronic homelessness, alongside family, youth and employment programs.
entries.how_to_access: Ask for Indigenous Housing First and confirm referral or eligibility rules.

entries.title: Veterans Affairs Canada — homelessness and emergency support
entries.description: Veterans and eligible family members can ask about housing help, case management and emergency funds for essentials. Every application is assessed and support is not guaranteed.
entries.how_to_access: Call and state that you are homeless or at risk of homelessness.

entries.title: Parachutes for Pets — Edmonton pet food and crisis support
entries.description: Pet-food hampers, essential supplies and referral-only short-term safekeeping for pets when a family faces a medical emergency, violence or housing instability. Stock and approval are not guaranteed.
entries.address: Edmonton pickup location provided through the program
entries.how_to_access: Complete the Edmonton request form for pet food. Safekeeping requires a professional referral; call the program for guidance.
